checked: OSU Kappler text: Treaty with the Creeks, Aug. 7, 1790, 7 Stat. 35, proclamation Aug. 13, 1790; Article 4 boundary, cession and $1,500 a year plus goods; Article 5 solemn guarantee of all Creek lands W. and S. of the line; Article 6 settlers forfeit US protection; Article 7 no hunting, passport required. Matches.

ICC Docket 275 (23 Ind. Cl. Comm. 1, Apr. 15, 1970, OSU id 927): Article 5 'was not intended to be a grant of legal rights of permanent occupancy' but 'an undertaking by the United States to protect the Creeks' aboriginal occupancy rights against incursions by the State of Georgia and white settlers'; neither the 1790 nor the 1814 treaty gave recognized title. The file's today states this accurately.

The Commission went on to find aboriginal title and order valuation as of April 8, 1816 under section 2(4); that claim rests on aboriginal title, not on a breach of this treaty, so no-breach-found stands.
